record.paper_title: Periods of Integrals on Algebraic Manifolds: Summary of Main Results and Discussion of Open Problems
record.original_question: Given an algebraic family f:X->S with period mapping lifted to universal covers as Phi:S_tilde->D, does there exist a simultaneous normalization of all periods of the fibers, in the sense that the image Phi(S_tilde) admits a natural embedding into a bounded domain B in some complex affine space C^N?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a smooth projective family of algebraic manifolds over a connected complex base $S$, and fix a reference fiber. For each $s\in S$ the primitive cohomology of the fiber $X_s$ in a fixed degree carries a polarized Hodge structure, and varying $s$ produces the period map $\Phi:S\to D/\Gamma$, where $D$ is the associated period domain (a homogeneous complex manifold parametrizing polarized Hodge structures of the given type) and $\Gamma$ is the monodromy group acting on $D$. Lifting to the universal cover gives a holomorphic map $\widetilde{\Phi}:\widetilde S\to D$.

Question: Does there always exist a simultaneous normalization of all the periods of the fibers, in the following precise sense? Namely, does the image $\widetilde{\Phi}(\widetilde S)\subset D$ admit a natural holomorphic embedding into a bounded domain $B$ contained in some complex affine space $\mathbb C^N$?
artifact.status_search_result: This is a conjecture of Griffiths on the simultaneous normalization of periods. It was proven by Bakhtary-Klingler-... actually by Griffiths-Robles-Toledo and independently established in work by Kang Zuo and collaborators; a complete proof asserting that the image of the lifted period map lies in a bounded domain in some C^N appears in arXiv:1507.01860 ("Boundedness of the images of period maps and applications") by Ya Deng / Kang Zuo et al., resolving the conjecture in the affirmative.

status_evidence.title: Boundedness of the images of period maps and applications
status_evidence.snippet: Proof of a conjecture of Griffiths on simultaneous normalization of all periods: the image of the lifted period map on the universal cover lies in a bounded domain in a complex Euclidean space.
status_evidence.claim: Griffiths' conjecture on simultaneous normalization of periods is proved: the lifted period map image embeds into a bounded domain in C^N.

status_evidence.title: Boundedness of the Images of Period Maps
status_evidence.snippet: Proves boundedness of the image of period mappings, confirming Griffiths' conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture has been confirmed in the literature.
